newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PEKAO SA PORTFOLIO DOWN IN Q2, AHEAD OF WIG.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PEKAO SA PORTFOLIO DOWN IN Q2, AHEAD OF WIG.

text.p: A model investment portfolio offered by Poland's Bank Pekao SA brokerage produced negative returns in the second quarter of 1997 but outperformed the bourse's main index, Pekao's research head said on Friday.

Jacek Stefanski told a news conference, the model portfolio adjusted montly by Pekao analysts and used by investors to shape their own portfolios, had a negative 4.24 percent return compared with a 6.3 percent drop in the all-share WIG index.
"Although there was a loss in this quarter, we are satisfied with the results because our rate (of return) is still above the WIG," Stefanski said.
He said that during the three quarters since its launch the portfolio produced a 84.26 percent return against the WIG's 2.27 percent gain.
Stefanski said the portfolio so far had been made of five to nine large cap companies listed on the main market.
"We didn't recommend our customers to buy on the primary market. First of all because of long waiting time and because it is risky," said Jacek Stefanski.

The portfolio's composition and the weighing of stocks is adjusted every month on the first trading day and Pekao SA customers can buy the proposed portfolio every month for a fixed price and follow its example in their own investments.
